headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill shifts certain electricity costs, including capacity procurement and distribution infrastructure, to large energy users like data centers, aiming to reduce residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, environmental advocates, some lawmakers (e.g., Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling).
opponents: Data center industry, large manufacturers, potentially Governor Spanberger (due to suggested weakening amendments).
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a key energy measure designed to shift more costs onto data centers and large manufacturers to save residential electricity customers money. The bill aims to allocate certain costs related to capacity procurement and distribution infrastructure investments to high-load users, potentially saving residential customers $5.52 a month.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill mandates that local water authorities report data center water consumption, making this information publicly accessible to increase transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (e.g., Virginia Conservation Network, Chesapeake Bay Foundation), Senator Kannan Srinivasan, concerned citizens.
opponents: Data center industry (though they state their water usage is low, they might oppose increased regulation).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public.
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, which will be publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency regarding the industry's water consumption, a growing concern among residents.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Assessments
short_summary: This bill mandates noise impact assessments for new data centers near residential areas and schools, and allows localities to require broader environmental and historical site impact assessments.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local governments, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups (e.g., Virginia Conservation Network, Piedmont Environmental Council), Delegate Joshua E. Thomas.
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased regulatory burden and potential siting restrictions).
news_headline: Data centers must provide noise impact assessments.
news_summary: HB 153 requires data centers to provide localities with a noise impact assessment on nearby residential areas and schools before approval of rezoning or special use permits. It also allows localities to require site assessments on potential impacts to water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forestland.
